title: Handmade gates craned into place at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester

input.lead: The new gates at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester replace ones installed more than 25 years ago
input.summary: The new gates at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester replace ones installed more than 25 years ago
input.evidence_text: Handmade gates craned into place at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester - BBC News Image source, PA Image caption, The new gates have come from Yorkshire, replacing locks that were more than 25 years old By Georgie Docker North West Published 1 hour ago Work has begun to restore lock gates across Greater Manchester's historical canal network. A team has started fitting new handmade gates at Lock 80 on the Rochdale Canal, a waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire. The new gates, at the lock to the east of the city centre in Manchester, were handcrafted from oak in Yorkshire, before being craned into place. Each leaf of the upstream gate weighs one-and-a-half tonnes (1,500 kg), and the downstream leaves weigh two-and-a-half tonnes (2,500 kg). They replace gates that were installed at the turn of the millennium. It comes after canal gates were replaced in the stretch of canal running through Manchester's Gay Village, in February. Image source, PA Image caption, The new locks are critical to keeping canals open, the Canal and River Trust said The Canal and River Trust, the charity that cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales, said the work was one of hundreds of projects over the next five months set to maintain the 2,000-mile canal network. This year's programme will see the replacement of 136 lock gate leaves – the individual doors or panels – as well as repairs to historic locks, bridges, embankments and other infrastructure. Elsewhere in the North West, there will also be repairs to five locks on the Marple Flight on the Peak Forest Canal in Greater Manchester and two locks on the Wigan Flight of the Leeds and Liverpool Canal in Lancashire. They labelled them a ‘backwards step’ for and an ‘unwelcome curtailing’ of democra Under the new rules planning applications would be split into two tiers – Schedule 1 applications and Schedule 2 applications, designated by planning officers. Schedule 1 includes smaller and more technical applications that would only be dealt with by planning officers Schedule 2 covers larger applications, which may be brought before the planning committee, if agreed by the planning committee chair and the council’s chief planning officer. The move also removes elected members’ right to ‘call in’ a planning application for scrutiny and debate The new rules came into force at the end of October, with Bury council now having approved the change in its constitution needed to meet the new legal requirements. The town hall owns around 7,600 homes with some 300 of these managed by an external agency It was the council’s first inspection under the regulatory framework and it was awarded a C3 rating – the second lowest outcome. The council took its housing services back into direct management in 2024 as it began to wind down social housing provider Six Town Housing (STH) It is in the process of consulting on the future of the remaining around 100 homes managed by STH, with a recent report recommending that these too be brought under the council control. Credit: Canal & River Trust / Spectrum Freight Ltd / Ote Lifting Ltd /Press Association Work is taking place to fit new lock gates in Manchester ’s historic Rochdale Can The Canal and River Trust, the charity that cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales , said it would be carrying out hundreds of projects over the next five months to maintain the “living heritage” of the network that was built in the industrial revolution and stil This year’s programme will see the replacement of lock gate leaves, the individual doors or panels as well as repairs to historic locks, bridges, embankments and other infrastructure Earlier this week, a team started fitting new lock gates at Lock 80 on the Rochdale Canal, a waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire The new gates, at the lock to the east of the city centre in Manchester, have been handcrafted from oak at the Canal and River Trust’s lock gate workshop at Stanley Ferry, Yorkshire, before being craned into place T he charity saidEach leaf of the upstream gate weighs 1.5 tonnes, and the downstream leaves weigh 2.5 tonnes, and replace gates that were installed around the turn of the millennium

The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area. The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications. Residents will be asked the following question: “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area. The deadline to register to vote is Tuesday 24 November 2026. Residents who wish to vote by post, proxy or who need a Voter Authority Certificate should also be aware of the following deadlines: - Wednesday 25 November, 5pm: Deadline for new postal vote applications and changes to existing postal voting arrangements. - Wednesday 2 December, 5pm: Deadline for new proxy vote applications and applications for a free Voter Authority Certificate. - Thursday 10 December, 5pm: Deadline for emergency proxy vote applications, where eligible. Residents can read the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan and supporting referendum documents online at: https://www.oldham.gov.uk/info/201235/neighbourhood_planning/2936/saddleworth_neighbourhood_plan Paper copies are also available to view at Lees, Uppermill, Delph and Greenfield libraries, Oldham Council’s reception

input.evidence_text: Sun 15th Nov, 2026 - Manchester City Joie Stadium Celebrities and football legends assemble for Game4Ricky charity match Manchester City Joie Stadium, North Gate, Etihad Campus, 400 Ashton New Rd, Manchester M11 4TQ Sun 15th Nov, 2026 2.15pm Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Some huge names from football, boxing and entertainment are heading to Manchester this November for Game4Ricky, a celebrity football match celebrating the life and legacy of Ricky Hatton Taking place on Sunday 15 November, the game will see Team Hatton face Team Hitman, with Ricky’s son Campbell Hatton and brother Matthew Hatton among those taking to the pitch. Kick-off is at 2.15pm, with the afternoon bringing together people from across the different worlds Ric Team Hatton currently includes Campbell Hatton alongside former Manchester City and England goalkeeper Joe Hart, actor Archie Renaux, former Lioness Toni Duggan, England legend Des Walker, former world champion boxer Paulie Malignaggi, comedian Jason Manford and presenter Harry P On the other side, Team Hitman features Matthew Hatton, former England goalkeeper David James, World Cup winner William Gallas, former England striker Natasha Dowie, Manchester City favourite Joleon Lescott, rapper Big Zuu, former world champion boxer Johnny Nelson and presenter More football legends, world champion sports stars, musicians and familiar faces from TV and entertainment are still to be announced ahead of the game

input.evidence_text: Sun 15th Nov, 2026 - Locations across Stockport town centre ©Matthew Nichol Photography Stockport’s Spectacular Sunday Locations across Stockport town centre Sun 15th Nov, 2026 12pm - 5pm Go to Manchester's Finest X profile A giant snow lion, a circus adventure into space and the world’s smallest nightclub. Stockport is kicking off Christmas in suitably weird and wonderful fashion, as Spectacular Sunday returns for its fourth year on Sunday 15 November More than 200 performers and 50 free shows will take over the town centre, transforming streets and squares into stages for giant puppets, circus acts, live music, comedy and all manner of festive surprises Among the highlights is the enormous Snow Lion, joined by dancing elves and towering stiltwalkers. There’s also Over The Moon, a circus adventure with an intergalactic twist, and Hydropunk, an interactive spectacle involving water-powered pipes, pumps, sprays and puzzles And if you fancy a rave between the Christmas shopping, The Miniscule of Sound, officially the world’s smallest nightclub, is back for another year. Expect big tunes in a very, very small space

On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. input.evidence_text: Events Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs: Become a Host Entrepreneur Erasmus for Young Entrepreneurs: Become a Host Entrepreneur Official Chamber Post FREE The University of Law Manchester , 2 New York St Manchester, M1 4HJ Friday 13 Nov 10am - 12pm Book Now Greater Manchester Cham The programme provides established business owners, founders and co-founders with an opportunity to host and mentor a developing entrepreneur from Europe. A matched entrepreneur can spend between one and three months collaborating with the host company, contributing fresh ideas, The visiting entrepreneur receives financial support through the programme and is responsible for arrangements including travel, accommodation, living expenses and insurance. There is no direct programme cost to the host business, although hosts are expected to make a personal co support your international growth ambitions; and develop your own leadership and mentoring experience The programme is designed as a collaborative exchange. The visiting entrepreneur works alongside the host business and contributes to its development, while the host shares practical entrepreneurial experience and guidance
